'''''Sedum morganianum''''', the '''donkey tail''' or '''burro's tail''', is  a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Crassulaceae, native to southern [[Mexico]]. It is a [[succulent plant|succulent]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] producing trailing stems up to {{convert|60|cm|0|abbr=on}} long, with fleshy blue-green leaves and terminal pink to red flowers in summer.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> ''S. morganianum'' has been found wild in two ravines at [[Tenampa]] county, in central [[Veracruz]], in eastern Mexico and on vertical cliffs of igneous rock in the Tropical Deciduous Forest zone. Due to its restricted geographic distribution, it should be regarded as a micro-endemic species.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Jimeno-Sevilla|first1=H. David|last2=Cházaro-Basáñez|first2=Miguel|last3=Albalat-Botana|first3=Amparo|date=2010-04-01|title=Reporte de una población silvestre de Sedum morganianum E. Walther (Crassulaceae)|journal=Acta Botanica Mexicana|issue=91|pages=13–20|doi=10.21829/abm91.2010.287|issn=2448-7589|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
With a minimum temperature of {{convert|5|-|7|C|F|abbr=on}}, in [[temperateness|temperate]] regions ''S. morganianum'' is often cultivated as a [[houseplant]] in a suspended container, with the trailing stems hanging down, vertically.<ref name=RHSAZ /> Alternatively, when the trailing stems are allowed to make prolonged, direct contact with the ground, or soil or other substrate (such as in an adjacent container), the [[leaf node|nodes]] will be triggered to root and attach, as is the case with numerous genera among the Crassulaceae.

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Sedum morganianum'' | url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/16969/Sedum-morganianum/Details | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 96 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 6 November 2018}}</ref>

''Sedum morganianum'' grows well outside in appropriate climates, provided frost is not a threat, in very good light but protected from the brightest portions of the day. Indoors, the plant is best grown in a window full of sunlight for strongest growth and to enhance leaf coloration. It requires regular, moderate watering all year, except in winter, when it should be infrequently watered. Excess irrigation and poor drainage can rot the plant in a short amount of time. If grown outside, this plant should also be sheltered from extreme heat and excess rainfall; the delicate and fragile leaves will fall from the plant extremely easily, often with the slightest touch, especially during rainstorms. However, even at high latitudes, removed or dropped leaves will readily propagate and produce roots, often rooting directly where they fall. These leaf propagations eventually form into new plants, especially if placed in a southern exposure (Northern Hemisphere) or northern exposure (Southern Hemisphere).

Plants are usually propagated by stem or leaf cuttings. The leaf attachment is quite loose, and leaves will often immediately break off of the stem when disturbed. The leaves will stay alive for many days and roots will emerge after a few days, especially with local humidity. Individual leaves will produce inches-long plants.

This plant exhibits a clearly visible [[Epicuticular wax#farina|wax layer]] (farina) on its leaves and stems, an indication of its preference for (bright) shade and sheltering from hot sun.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wollenweber|first1=Eckhard|last2=Doerr|first2=Marion|last3=Siems|first3=Karsten|last4=Faure|first4=Robert|last5=Bombarda|first5=Isabelle|last6=Gaydou|first6=Emile M|date=January 1999|title=Triterpenoids in lipophilic leaf and stem coatings|journal=Biochemical Systematics and Ecology|volume=27|issue=1|pages=103–105|doi=10.1016/s0305-1978(98)00070-2|bibcode=1999BioSE..27..103W |issn=0305-1978}}</ref>
